'''Juan José Giambiagi''' (18 June 1924 &ndash; 8 January 1996) was an Argentine theoretical physicist. He was professor of the [[University of Buenos Aires]] but after a series of [[coup d'état]]s in Argentina, he moved to Brazil. He is known for the discovery of [[dimensional regularization]] in [[quantum field theory]].

== Life ==
Juan José Giambiagi was born in [[Buenos Aires]] in 1924.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bes |first=Daniel |date=1996 |title=Juan José Giambiagi Biografía |url=https://www.df.uba.ar/en/actividades-y-servicios/hemeroteca/6613-juan-jose-giambiagi |access-date=2025-06-07 |website=Universidad de Buenos Aires Departamento de Física |language=es}}</ref> studied at the [[University of Buenos Aires]] (UBA) graduating in 1948, and obtaining a doctorate in physics in 1950.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Juan José Giambiagi (1924 - 1996) — ICTP Portal |url=https://portal.ictp.it/icts/facilities/lecture_rooms/AGH/giambiagi/giambiagi_biography |access-date=2025-06-07 |website=portal.ictp.it}}</ref> His thesis was titled "Application of the Hadamard method to some problems in [[mathematical physics]]" ({{Langx|es|Aplicación del método de Hadamard a algunos problemas de físicomatemática}})<ref name=":0" /> and his PhD advisor was [[Alberto González Domínguez]].<ref name=":1" />

He became faculty of UBA from 1957 to 1956.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Bietenholz |first=Wolfgang |last2=Prado |first2=Lilian |date=2014-02-01 |title=Revolutionary physics in reactionary Argentina |url=https://doi.org/10.1063/PT.3.2277 |journal=Physics Today |volume=67 |issue=2 |pages=38–43 |doi=10.1063/PT.3.2277 |issn=0031-9228}}</ref> Under his direction, physicist [[Miguel Ángel Virasoro (physicist)|Miguel Ángel Virasoro]] was recruited.<ref name=":1" />

In 1960, Giambiagi, [[José Leite Lopes]] from Brazil and [[Marcos Moshinsky]] from Mexico, founded the Centro Latino-Americano de Física (CLAF).<ref name=":1" />

After the [[Argentine Revolution]] of 1966, General [[Juan Carlos Onganía]] dissolved university autonomy and chased academics opposed to his regime.<ref name=":1" /> Due to these events,  69 of the 75 professors and researchers of the School of Exact and Natural Sciences of UBA had resigned, including Giambiagi.<ref name=":1" /> Along with his collaborator [[Carlos Guido Bollini]] and two other professors, Giambiagi a wrote a letter in the Argentine newspaper ''[[La Nación]]'' to condemn the attack on universities.<ref name=":1" />

Giambiagi and Bollini continued to work outside of UBA. From 1968 to 1976 they worked in the math department of the [[National University of La Plata]], which at the time was smaller and underfunded.<ref name=":1" /> Despite the issues, this period was considered their most productive period.<ref name=":1" />

In 1973, Giambiagi was arrested for alleged participation on Jewish or communist conspiracies.<ref name=":1" /> However he was released for his collaborations with the United States government during his time at UBA.<ref name=":1" />

After the [[1976 Argentine coup d'état]], the University of La Plata was targeted by the new authorities.<ref name=":1" /> That year, Giambiagi was detained again and interrogated.<ref name=":1" /> After being released, Giambiagi escaped with his family to Brazil. Giambiagi started working in [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas]], as head of the particle-physics department from 1978 to 1985.<ref name=":1" />

In 1986, Giambiagi became the director of CLAF.<ref name=":1" />

Giamgiagi was an early supporter of the creation of the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) and was in ICTP Scientific Council from 1987 to 1995.<ref name=":0" />

Giambiagi died in 1996 in [[Rio de Janeiro]].<ref name=":1" />

== Work on dimensional regularization ==
In 1971, Giambiagi and [[Carlos Guido Bollini]], published the first work on [[dimensional regularization]].<ref name=":1" /> Their method allows to treat divergent integrals. It consist in calculating the integrals in ''d'' = 4 + ''ε'' dimensions and later take the limit ''ε'' → 0 only at the very end.<ref name=":1" /> Their work was inspired by Giambiagi's [[doctoral advisor]] Alberto González Domínguez on [[analytical regularization]].<ref name=":1" /> Giambiagi and Bollini tried to publish in [[Physics Letters|''Physics Letters B'']] in 1971 but their work was rejected by the referees.<ref name=":1" /> Their work was later accepted, in August 1972,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bollini |first=C. G. |last2=Giambiagi |first2=J. J. |date=1972-08-07 |title=Lowest order “divergent” graphs in v-dimensional space |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0370269372904832 |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=40 |issue=5 |pages=566–568 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(72)90483-2 |issn=0370-2693|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and in [[Nuovo Cimento|''Il'' ''Nuovo Cimento'']] in November 1972.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bollini |first=C. G. |last2=Giambiagi |first2=J. J. |date=November 1972 |title=Dimensional renorinalization : The number of dimensions as a regularizing parameter |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02895558 |journal=Il Nuovo Cimento B |language=en |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=20–26 |doi=10.1007/BF02895558 |issn=1826-9877|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Meanwhile, [[Gerard 't Hooft]] and [[Martinus J. G. Veltman]] independently discovered dimensional regularization but got their paper published in July 1972 before Giambiagi and Bollini.<ref>{{Cite journal |last='t Hooft |first=G. |last2=Veltman |first2=M. |date=1972-07-01 |title=Regularization and renormalization of gauge fields |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0550321372902799 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=44 |issue=1 |pages=189–213 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(72)90279-9 |issn=0550-3213}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Veltman admitted to have seen drafts of Giambiagi and Bollini's work.<ref name=":1" />

Both t' Hooft and Veltman were awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] in 1999 for "elucidating the quantum structure of electroweak interactions in physics.”, but the work of Giambiagi and Bollini was not cited in the document references.<ref name=":1" /> However, Veltman mentioned “the independent work of Bollini and Giambiagi,” in his Nobel lecture.<ref name=":1" />

== Honors and awards ==
After the death of Giambiagi, the physics department at UBA was renamed the Juan José Giambiagi Department of Physics.<ref name=":1" /> At ICTP, the Giambiagi lecture hall was created.<ref name=":1" />
